result.topic_en: Euler attempts to determine the true place of the lunar node and the true inclination of the Moon's orbit from eclipse observations, compares several formulas that give inconsistent node positions, finds a correction of 5'47" to the tabular node, and proposes using partial eclipses (the tenth eclipse, 1731 June 19) to determine the inclination.
result.transcription:
De vero loco nodi atque vera inclinatione orbitae lunaris ad eclipticam. 379
erit valor vero proximus . . . . . . $x = 6^s\, 4^0\, 16'\, 43''$
seu a nodo descendente computando $x = \quad 4\;\, 16\;\, 43$
quem valorem autem nunc accuratius definiri oportet.
§ 5. Deinde cum inclinatio orbitae lunaris ad eclipticam jam prope sit
$\varrho = 5^0\, 16'\, 54''$
erit ejus semissis $\tfrac{1}{2}\varrho = 2\;\, 38\;\, 27$
et distantiae $x$ duplum $2x = 8\;\, 33\;\, 26$
unde quaeratur angulus ille parvus $c = \frac{(m+n+2k)\sin 2x \tang^2 \frac{1}{2}\varrho}{g(n-m)}$ sec. existente $lg = 4{,}6855749$,
qui invenitur $c = 75'' = 1'\, 15''$.
Tum quaerantur porro anguli: $a+b = 3993'' = 1^0\, 6'\, 33''$ ; $a+b+c = 1^0\, 7'\, 48''$
$A+B = 1268 \;= 0\;\, 21\;\, 8$ ; $A+B+c = 0\;\, 22\;\, 23$
$a-b = 3491 \;= 0\;\, 58\;\, 11$ ; $a-b+c = 0\;\, 59\;\, 26$
$A-B = 1108 \;= 0\;\, 18\;\, 28$ ; $A-B+c = 0\;\, 19\;\, 43$
et anguli $f = 1\;\, 1\;\, 17$ $\qquad F = 0\;\, 28\;\, 2$
ex quibus quaeratur $d = \frac{\cos f - \cos^2\frac{1}{2}\varrho\cos(a-b+c)}{\cos F - \cos^2\frac{1}{2}\varrho\cos(A-B+c)}$ fietque $ld = 0{,}001647$, et cum sit
$\tang 2x = \frac{d\cos(A+B+c) - \cos(a+b+c)}{\sin(a+b+c) - d\sin(A+B+c)}$
hinc autem reperitur $x = 8^0 22' 45''$, qui valor fere duplo est major, quam ex tabulis invenitur.
Sin autem utamur formula
$\cos(2x - a - b - c) = \frac{\cos f - \cos^2\frac{1}{2}\varrho\cos(a-b+c)}{\sin^2\frac{1}{2}\varrho}$
invenitur $x = 3^0\, 19'\, 59''$; unde patet ex his formulis nimis esse lubricum locum nodi assignare.
§ 6. Certior videtur formula alia supra inventa
$\frac{\cos(a+b) + \sin(a+b)\tang(2x-c)}{\cos(a+b) - \sin(a+b)\tang(2x-c)} = \frac{\cos f - \cos^2\frac{1}{2}\varrho\cos(a-b+c)}{\cos f - \cos^2\frac{1}{2}\varrho\cos(a-b-c)}$
ex qua calculo subducto reperitur $2x = 8^0 21' 52''$ et $x = 4^0 10' 56''$, qui valor ab eo, quem tabulae exhibent $x = 4^0 16' 43''$ deficit $5' 47''$, ita ut locus nodi medius hac particula $5' 47''$ promovendus videatur. Hac autem correctione adhibita, cum sit
$\sin^2\frac{1}{2}\varrho = \frac{\cos(a-b+c) - \cos f}{2\sin(x-a-c)\sin(x-b)} = \frac{\sin\frac{f+a-b+c}{2}\sin\frac{f-a+b-c}{2}}{\sin(x-a-c)\sin(x-b)}$
hi autem anguli nimis sunt parvi, quam ut inde inclinatio vera recte concludi possit.
§ 7. Quoniam si hac ultima methodo utamur, immersionis et emersionis nulla ratio habetur, eclipses quoque partiales ad hunc scopum adhibere poterimus, quae etiam erunt aptiores ad inclinationem definiendam, cum anguli in denominatore $x-a-c$ et $x-b$ non fiant adeo parvi.
Sumamus ergo eclipsin decimam
A. 1731 Jun. $19^d$ init. $13^h 14' 21''$ fin. $14\;\, 40\;\, 41$ medium $13^h 57' 31''$ t. v.
at medium A. 1731 Jun. $19^d$ $13^h 58' 15''$ tempore medio.

items.quote: quem valorem autem nunc accuratius definiri oportet.
items.english: But this value must now be determined more accurately.

items.quote: unde patet ex his formulis nimis esse lubricum locum nodi assignare.
items.english: Whence it is clear that assigning the place of the node from these formulas is too unreliable.

items.quote: ita ut locus nodi medius hac particula $5' 47''$ promovendus videatur.
items.english: So that the mean place of the node seems to need advancing by this small amount of 5'47".

items.quote: hi autem anguli nimis sunt parvi, quam ut inde inclinatio vera recte concludi possit.
items.english: But these angles are too small for the true inclination to be correctly deduced from them.

items.quote: eclipses quoque partiales ad hunc scopum adhibere poterimus, quae etiam erunt aptiores ad inclinationem definiendam
items.english: We shall also be able to use partial eclipses for this purpose, which will be even more suitable for determining the inclination.
